attributes.residual: Reduced from the superseded record's '9 STRUCTURAL rows, source-reachable' to ONE mechanism plus one symbol-identity finding. MECHANISM (parked by law): at 0x308 the target emits an unfused pair `bne ->0x310` / `b ->0x1a0` where we emit a single folded `beq ->0x1a0`; that is the entire instruction-count gap (target 272, ours 271) and the sole cause of every CFG-BRANCH-TARGET row. 0x1a0 was verified to be the top of the main service loop (`li r3,-5` / `bl serve_busy` / `bl sndFxQueUpdate`), reached by fallthrough from 0x19c and by this one backward branch - i.e. the `b` IS the loop back branch, the backedge variant, which the governing law states MWCC always folds. Not source-reachable; do not spend probes on it. SEPARATE FINDING, symbol identity, NOT parked: at target 0x318 the relocation names `sFlags` where our object names `gControllerButtons+0x4`. Both name the same address, so this is a relocation-symbol difference rather than a byte difference, but it is scored. Cause: screensaver.c:134 declares `extern s64 gControllerButtons;` - an 8-byte declaration - so the low word of the 64-bit AND falls INSIDE our gControllerButtons symbol, whereas the target treats the word at +4 as the separate 4-byte global `sFlags` (screensaver.c:135, `extern u32 sFlags;`). Deliberately NOT acted on: gControllerButtons and sFlags are cross-TU symbols, sFlags is an unresolved group-D row in claim.HW_externcheck-defect-table-worked-state.20260901.v1 ('NEEDS TARGET EVIDENCE, 16 all-NonMatching rows'), and retyping either is outside this TU-scoped claim and would require the rename-symbol procedure. Recorded here as the target-asm access-width evidence that group-D row was waiting for: the target's own relocation proves the word at gControllerButtons+4 is a distinct 4-byte symbol, so gControllerButtons is NOT 8 bytes wide.
